Among the many Apple Intelligence features rolling out with iOS 27, the Passwords app is getting a particularly powerful one: it can automatically change your passwords for you.

With Apple Intelligence, the Passwords app will be able to automatically fix your compromised login credentials on iOS 27.

Brand-new Apple Intelligence will be at the heart of the upcoming iOS 27 and related software updates. One powerful new AI feature directly tied to Apple's Passwords app.

When the Passwords app launched two years ago, it already served as a dedicated hub for centrally managing login credentials, two-factor authentication codes, Wi-Fi passwords, passkeys, and more.

If any password in your database has an issue, the app has always alerted you. For example, if your password turns up in a data breach or is reused across multiple accounts, the Passwords app will let you know.

However, until now, you have still had to manually fix these problematic credentials yourself.

But Apple says that in iOS 27, their brand-new agentic AI capabilities can change your passwords for you in a variety of situations. According to the official website:

This feature lets you ensure your login credentials are always secure, using passwords strong enough for the job, while minimising the actions and time required.

iOS 27 is currently in beta and is expected to roll out to all users in the coming weeks. The brand-new Passwords feature is expected to debut in iOS 27.0, but its stability in beta has been poor, so it may be delayed until iOS 27.1.

Have you tried the brand-new Passwords feature in the iOS 27 beta? How was your experience? Let us know in the comments.
